section_1.title: The Big Picture: Static vs. Dynamic
section_1.content: Introduce the fundamental limitation of basic algebra: it works perfectly for constant rates but fails when things change continuously. Define calculus as the mathematical language for describing change and accumulation. Use a visual comparison between a straight ramp and a curved slide.
section_1.example: A turtle moves at a constant 1m/s (Algebra), versus a playful puppy whose speed fluctuates as it chases a butterfly (Calculus).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Magic of 'Almost Zero'
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of 'Limits' and 'Approximation'. Explain that by looking at smaller and smaller intervals, we can treat a complex curve as a series of tiny straight lines. This sets the stage for the 'Infinitesimal'.
section_2.example: A circle being approximated by an inscribed polygon. As the number of sides increases, the 'gap' between the polygon and the circle vanishes toward zero.

section_3.title: Differentiation: The Art of Zooming In
section_3.content: Explain differentiation as finding the 'instantaneous' rate of change. Visually, this is represented by zooming into a curve until it appears to be a straight line. Introduce the 'Slope' at a single point (Tangent line).
section_3.example: A cheetah mid-sprint. While we know its average speed, differentiation tells us its exact velocity at the precise micro-second its paw hits the ground.

section_4.title: Integration: The Art of Slicing and Adding
section_4.content: Define integration as the reverse process: finding the total 'whole' by summing up infinite tiny 'parts'. Visually, show the area under a curve being filled with thinner and thinner rectangular slices (Riemann Sums).
section_4.example: Calculating the total amount of water in a leaking bucket. We don't know the total, but we know the 'rate' of the drip. By adding up every tiny drop over time, we find the total volume lost.

section_5.title: The Grand Connection: The Fundamental Theorem
section_5.content: The 'Essence' of calculus: Integration and Differentiation are inverse operations. Show a dynamic graph where the rate at which the 'Area' grows (Integration) is exactly equal to the 'Height' of the graph at that point (Differentiation).
section_5.example: A robotic arm painting a wall. The speed at which the arm moves (Derivative) determines how much area is covered (Integral). If you know one, you can mathematically find the other.

section_6.title: Summary: Calculus in the Real World
section_6.content: Wrap up by emphasizing that calculus allows us to model everything from planetary orbits to the spread of a virus. It is the bridge between a frozen snapshot and a moving reality.
section_6.example: Animation of a rocket launch: Calculus calculates the fuel consumption (change in mass) to ensure the rocket reaches the exact orbital height (accumulation of distance).

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Prerequisite: The Magic of 'Almost Zero'"
        lines = [
            "We approximate complex curves using tiny straight intervals.",
            "Increasing these intervals makes the approximation much more accurate.",
            "As intervals shrink toward zero, the true shape emerges."

        COLOR_POLYGON = "#FF00FF"

        # The .replace() matches dimensions, keeping it inside. 
        # Since replace uses bounding box, it might be slightly off for perfect inscribed.
        # We manually scale it slightly to fit inside the circle's radius.
        hexagon.scale(0.95) 

        self.play(Create(circle), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Create(hexagon), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2.0)

        self.play(Transform(hexagon, poly_12), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(Transform(hexagon, poly_24), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(Transform(hexagon, poly_48), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the vanishing gap with a yellow #FFFF00 arrow and the label 'Limit'.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_LIMIT)
        
        # Position for the arrow: pointing at the tiny gap between circle and polygon
        # Circle center is at the center of B2-E5.
        center_point = (self.grid["B2"] + self.grid["E5"]) / 2
        # Arrow starts slightly outside and points to a point on the circle
        arrow_start = center_point + np.array([2.2, 1.2, 0])
        arrow_end = center_point + np.array([1.3, 0.8, 0])
        
        limit_arrow = Arrow(
            start=arrow_start, 
            end=arrow_end, 
            color=COLOR_LIMIT, 
            buff=0.1,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        limit_label = Text("Limit", font_size=24, color=COLOR_LIMIT)
        # Position label near arrow start (following proximity rule L002)
        # Scaling label for L002
        limit_label.scale(0.8)
        limit_label.next_to(limit_arrow, UP, buff=0.2)

        self.play(Create(limit_arrow))
        self.play(Write(limit_label))
        
        # Use Indicate for the highlight (L004)
        self.play(Indicate(limit_label), Indicate(limit_arrow))
        
        self.wait(2.0)

        # Execute the race (4 seconds for clarity)
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2.0)

        func = lambda x: 0.8 * np.sin(x - p_coords[0]) + p_coords[1]
        curve = FunctionGraph(func, x_range=[p_coords[0]-2.5, p_coords[0]+2.5], color="#00FFFF")
        curve.set_stroke(width=4)
        
        dot_p = Dot(p_coords, color="#FFFFFF")
        label_p = MathTex("P", color="#FFFFFF").scale(0.8)

        self.add(curve, dot_p, label_p)
        self.play(Create(curve), FadeIn(dot_p), Write(label_p))

        # Highlight the concept of derivative as slope at a point
        self.play(
            Indicate(slope_label),

            run_time=2.0
        )
        
        # Subtle pulse of the tangent line to emphasize the 'velocity'
        self.play(

        )

        self.setup_layout("The Grand Connection: The Fundamental Theorem", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Morph a large white 'Σ' symbol into a magenta '∫' symbol #FF00FF. Then self.wait(2.0).
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        sigma = MathTex(r"\Sigma", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=120)
        integral = MathTex(r"\int", color="#FF00FF", font_size=120)
        
        # Position in a central area on the right
        self.place_in_area(sigma, "B3", "D4")
        self.place_in_area(integral, "B3", "D4")
        
        self.play(Write(sigma))
        self.wait(1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(sigma, integral))
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a graph where a moving white vertical line #FFFFFF highlights the 'Height' at each point. Then self.wait(2.0).
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        self.play(FadeOut(integral))
        
        # Graph setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"color": "#FFFFFF", "include_tip": False}
        )
        
        func = lambda x: 0.2 * x**2 + 0.5
        graph = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 3.5], color="#00FFFF")
        
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, graph)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph))
        
        # Value tracker for interactive movement
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(1)
        
        # Height line (persistent + updater to avoid always_redraw overhead)
        height_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(1, 0),
            axes.c2p(1, func(1)),
            color="#FFFFFF"
        )
        height_line.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0),
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value()))
        ))
        
        # Label following the line
        height_label = MathTex("f(x)", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=28)
        height_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(height_line, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(Create(height_line), Write(height_label))
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # One operation undoes the effect of the other.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Area growth - using always_redraw for the complex polygon shape
        area = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_area(
            graph, x_range=[0, x_tracker.get_value()], color="#FF00FF", opacity=0.3
        ))
        
        self.add(area)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(3), run_time=4)
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Use a green #00FF00 arrow to link the moving 'Height' to the growth of the 'Total Area'. Then self.wait(2.0).
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # Arrow from height to area
        arrow = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(3, func(3) + 0.5), 
            end=axes.c2p(1.5, 0.5), 
            color="#00FF00", 
            buff=0.1
        )
        
        area_label = Text("Total Area", color="#00FF00", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, "F4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow), Write(area_label))
        self.play(Indicate(arrow)) # Using L004 Indicate
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # It bridges the gap between change and accumulation.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        self.play(Indicate(height_line), Indicate(area))
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # Reset and conclude
        self.play(self.lecture.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2.0)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Use the provided TeachingScene base class without modification.
class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Metadata retrieved from shared state
        title_text = "Summary: Calculus in the Real World"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Calculus models everything from rocket launches to viruses.",
            "It transforms frozen snapshots into a moving reality.",
            "Master change and you master the language of nature."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Hexadecimal colors (L008)
        COLOR_ROCKET = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_TRAJECTORY = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_VELOCITY = "#FF8000"
        COLOR_ORBIT = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_CALCULUS = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a white #FFFFFF rocket launching and following a cyan #00FFFF parabolic trajectory.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_ROCKET))
        
        # Simple Rocket mobject: Body and Nose
        rocket_body = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=0.4, color=COLOR_ROCKET, fill_opacity=1)
        rocket_nose = Triangle(color=COLOR_ROCKET, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.12).next_to(rocket_body, UP, buff=0)
        rocket = VGroup(rocket_body, rocket_nose)
        
        # Start at grid F2 to avoid lecture text (L002)
        self.place_at_grid(rocket, "F2", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        start_pt = self.grid["F2"]
        end_pt = self.grid["C5"]
        # Approximate a parabola with an arc for smooth motion
        trajectory = ArcBetweenPoints(start_pt, end_pt, angle=-TAU/8).set_color(COLOR_TRAJECTORY)
        
        # Orient rocket for launch direction
        rocket.rotate(-45 * DEGREES) 
        
        self.play(Create(trajectory), run_time=1.5)
        # Rocket follows the arc path
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(rocket, trajectory), run_time=2.5, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(2.0) # L010: Absorption time for learner

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash the word 'Velocity' in orange #FF8000 at multiple points along the trajectory.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_VELOCITY))
        
        v_labels = VGroup(
            Text("Velocity", font_size=20, color=COLOR_VELOCITY),
            Text("Velocity", font_size=20, color=COLOR_VELOCITY),
            Text("Velocity", font_size=20, color=COLOR_VELOCITY)
        )
        
        # Position labels following Proximity Rule (L002)
        proportions = [0.2, 0.5, 0.8]
        for i, prop in enumerate(proportions):
            pt = trajectory.point_from_proportion(prop)
            v_labels[i].move_to(pt + RIGHT * 0.8 + UP * 0.2)
            self.play(FadeIn(v_labels[i]))
            self.play(Indicate(v_labels[i], color=COLOR_VELOCITY)) # L004: Visual highlighting
        
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rocket reaches a circular yellow #FFFF00 orbit while the word 'Calculus' appears in glowing white #FFFFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ORBIT))
        
        # Target orbit centered at B4
        orbit_center_pos = self.grid["B4"]
        orbit_radius = 1.0
        orbit_circle = Circle(radius=orbit_radius, color=COLOR_ORBIT).move_to(orbit_center_pos)
        
        # Clear previous markers
        self.play(FadeOut(trajectory), FadeOut(v_labels))
        
        # Move rocket to the orbital entry point
        orbit_entry = orbit_circle.point_from_proportion(0)
        self.play(
            rocket.animate.move_to(orbit_entry).rotate(45 * DEGREES), # Re-orient to "up"
            Create(orbit_circle),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Centerpiece text
        calculus_label = Text("Calculus", font_size=36, color=COLOR_CALCULUS)
        self.place_at_grid(calculus_label, "B4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Low-complexity updater for orbital motion (L027)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        rocket.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(orbit_circle.point_from_proportion(angle_tracker.get_value() % 1)))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(calculus_label), Indicate(calculus_label, color=COLOR_CALCULUS))
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Clean up and finalize
        rocket.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(2.0)

outline.title: Differentiation: The Art of Zooming In
outline.content: Explain differentiation as finding the 'instantaneous' rate of change. Visually, this is represented by zooming into a curve until it appears to be a straight line. Introduce the 'Slope' at a single point (Tangent line).
outline.example: A cheetah mid-sprint. While we know its average speed, differentiation tells us its exact velocity at the precise micro-second its paw hits the ground.

outline.title: Integration: The Art of Slicing and Adding
outline.content: Define integration as the reverse process: finding the total 'whole' by summing up infinite tiny 'parts'. Visually, show the area under a curve being filled with thinner and thinner rectangular slices (Riemann Sums).
outline.example: Calculating the total amount of water in a leaking bucket. We don't know the total, but we know the 'rate' of the drip. By adding up every tiny drop over time, we find the total volume lost.

storyboard.title: Differentiation: The Art of Zooming In
lecture_lines: Differentiation finds the exact rate of change right now.
Zoom into any smooth curve far enough.
Eventually, the curve looks like a simple straight line.
This line's slope is the derivative at that point.
It measures instantaneous velocity in a single micro-second.
animations: Draw a cyan #00FFFF curve and mark a specific point P with a white #FFFFFF dot. Then self.wait(2.0).
Smoothly zoom into point P for 5 seconds until the local curve segment appears as a straight line. Then self.wait(2.0).
Draw an orange #FF8000 tangent line at point P and label it 'Slope' alongside the icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/v.svg]. Then self.wait(2.0).

storyboard.title: Integration: The Art of Slicing and Adding
lecture_lines: Integration calculates the total by summing up small parts.
Imagine slicing the area under a curve into rectangles.
Thinner rectangles provide a more precise total area.
